about.title: Westmorland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Westmorland is a small community, but its roads still see real collisions — public records show injury crashes along corridors like Rt 85, 6th Street, 8th Street, and W Main Street, with a noticeable cluster of reports on Monday nights into early Tuesday morning. When a crash happens here, the aftermath can feel overwhelming: medical visits, missed work, calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. We handle personal injury claims for Westmorland residents, evaluating the crash, dealing with insurers, and explaining your options under California law. Acting early matters, since evidence like skid marks, vehicle damage, and witness memories fade fast in a town this size. There's no obligation and no upfront cost to find out where you stand.
commonInjuries: Cuts, bruises, and soft tissue damage

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Deadline Is Real
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a county road agency) is involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible for the crash. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to shift blame onto you, which is why it's worth speaking to an attorney first.

items.title: No Cap on What You're Owed for Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in most car accident cases. We work on contingency — no fee unless you recover — and can help make sure that value isn't underestimated.

items.question: I was in a crash on Rt 85 near Westmorland — do I really need a lawyer for a small town accident?
items.answer: Even in a small community like Westmorland, insurance companies handle claims the same way they would anywhere else, often looking for ways to limit what they pay. We can review the details of your crash, including police reports and any witness accounts, and let you know if pursuing a claim makes sense. There's no cost to have that conversation.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called me — should I give them a statement?
items.answer: It's generally best not to give a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since anything you say can be used later to reduce or deny your claim. Insurers often ask leading questions early, while you're still dealing with injuries and shock. We can talk to the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Westmorland car accident?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit, but if a government entity or public road agency is potentially involved, that deadline can be as short as six months. Because the timeline can vary, it's worth getting a free case review sooner rather than later so you don't lose your options.
